moments.selftext: Marble hands sculpted by Michelangelo at age 26 and Bernini at age 23. The comparison between Michelangelo’s marble hands, sculpted at age twenty-six, and Gian Lorenzo Bernini’s work at twenty-three reveals two different approaches to portraying the human form. In David, Michelangelo displayed extraordinary anatomical precision, rendering veins, tendons, and muscular tension to convey both physical strength and intellectual power. Bernini took marble in an equally remarkable direction with The Rape of Proserpina. His depiction of Pluto’s fingers pressing into Proserpina’s thigh creates the astonishing illusion of soft flesh yielding beneath his grip. Where Michelangelo used marble to express idealized human perfection, Bernini transformed it into something remarkably lifelike and tactile.

moments.selftext: A missing drunk man spent hours helping a search party look for himself. A 50-year-old intoxicated man named Beyhan Mutlu from Bursa Province, Turkey, accidentally joined a search party looking for him. After a night of heavy drinking with friends, Mutlu wandered into a nearby forest around İnegöl and never returned home, prompting his wife and friends to contact authorities. Police and volunteers soon began searching the dense woods. Still heavily intoxicated, Mutlu encountered the rescue team but mistakenly thought they were searching for someone else. He joined the group, walked with them for hours, and even called out the missing person’s name alongside the rescuers. The bizarre situation finally ended when a rescuer shouted Mutlu’s full name. Mutlu reportedly responded, “Who are we looking for? I am here.” Authorities then escorted him home safely, turning what began as a missing-person search into one of the strangest rescue stories imaginable.
